detail.longDescription: I'm building a web-based text/font tool where users can enter Unicode characters and preview them using different font families. The problem is that not every font supports every Unicode character. When a character isn't available in the selected font, the browser may silently use a fallback font, which makes it difficult to know whether the original font actually contains that glyph. For example: Hello ★ こんにちは Some characters may come from Arial, while others may be rendered using a fallback font. Is there a reliable way in JavaScript or the browser APIs to determine whether a specific font actually supports a given Unicode character? Ideally, I'd like to do something similar to: supportsCharacter("Arial", "★"); // true/false supportsCharacter("Arial", "あ"); // true/false I've considered comparing rendered text widths using canvas.measureText() , but I'm not sure whether that is reliable because of browser font fallback. Is there a standard browser API for checking glyph availability, or is measuring/rendering against a known fallback font the usual approach?
